chapter: Instruments, first jobs and the regional scene
title: Brass bands and parades around Baton Rouge
summary: Joe envied the Clayborn Williams band and recalls Firemen's and circus parades on North Boulevard and a band at Crackamon.

story.theme_name: Brass bands, parades and jazz funerals
story.community_name: Parading for Mardi Gras and the clubs

blocks.x: No. Because I never played with any big bands when I was a kid. That's one thing I wish they would have had, a kind of a brass band in Baton Rouge where I could play. And I used to feel a little jealous when... They had a band out of Daumersonville(?), Louisiana, called Clayborn Williams, which was a great band. Old man Clayborn Williams. His son George just died here; he was a good piano player.

Well, they had a big parade in Baton Rouge. Like I said, in Baton Rouge there was a big thoroughfare, North Boulevard, and all the circus parades... Any parade, any event that had a parade or something, North Boulevard was the street, they'd come down North Boulevard

and circle North Boulevard and go around Devlindon(?) Street -- that's another street they'd go down. And Third Street was the main street in Baton Rouge downtown. So every year they had a parade called the Firemen's Parade, which was almost compared to, say, a Fourth of July Parade or something. But the Fireman's Parade was I think a benefit for the firemen or something; they'd bring in some of these bands or something like that.
How far was Daumersonville(?) from Baton Rouge?

Daumersonville(?) was across the river, going to new Orleans, maybe twenty miles from Baton Rouge. And Crackamon(?), Louisiana, was another town, maybe ten miles from Daumersonville(?), that had a good band called The Blue Devils. I think Evan Thomas was in that band at one time.
